cues.text: A Host Dropped on Christmas Day
On Christmas Day, December 25, 2013, during the distribution of Holy Communion at St. Hyacinth's Church in Legnica, Poland, a consecrated Host fell to the floor.
Following standard Church practice, the priest placed it in a vasculum, a container of water meant to let the Host dissolve naturally over time, and set it in the tabernacle.
Rather than dissolving as expected, the Host developed a red stain over the following days.

Bishop Stefan Cichy of Legnica, informed of the phenomenon, established a diocesan commission to monitor and investigate it; in February 2014, a small fragment of the discolored tissue was set aside on a corporal and submitted for forensic examination.
Tissue Consistent With a Dying Heart
Independent testing by forensic medicine departments at universities in Wroclaw and Szczecin identified fragmented cross-striated muscle tissue, most closely resembling cardiac muscle.
DNA analysis confirmed the tissue was human in origin.
The cellular alteration pattern was consistent with tissue under severe physiological distress, comparable to findings reported for the Lanciano, Sokolka, and Buenos Aires accounts.
Bishop Zbigniew Kiernikowski, who succeeded Bishop Cichy in the diocese, presented the completed findings to the Vatican's Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith in January 2016.
On April 10 that year, following guidance from the Holy See, he formally announced to the diocese that the event bore the hallmarks of a Eucharistic miracle.
He ordered a suitable place prepared in St. Hyacinth's for the faithful to venerate the relic.

On July 2, 2016, more than three thousand of the faithful attended a liturgy of expiation in the Legnica cathedral before processing to St. Hyacinth's, where the relic was installed in a reliquary on the church's main altar.
Bishop Kiernikowski described the sign as an act of God's love and humility, coming to humanity in what he called ultimate self-humbling.
This closed the formal diocesan process, three years after a single dropped Host on a Christmas morning, with a relic now permanently enshrined for public veneration.
